eiffel: The tower is 330 metres (1,083 ft) tall, about the same height as an 81-storey building, and the tallest structure in Paris.
It is named after the engineer Gustave Eiffel, whose company designed and built the tower from 1887 to 1889.
greatwall: Successive dynasties expanded the wall system; the best-known sections were built by the Ming dynasty (1368–1644).
The first walls date to the 7th century BC; these were joined together in the Qin dynasty.
everest: In 1856, Andrew Waugh announced Everest (then known as Peak XV) as 8,840 m (29,002 ft) high, after several years of calculations based on observations made by the Great Trigonometrical Survey.
Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary made the first documented ascent of Everest in 1953, using the Southeast Ridge route.
telephone: Alexander Graham Bell was the first to be awarded a patent for the electric telephone by the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) in March 1876.
The first telephone patent was granted to Alexander Graham Bell in 1876.
curie: Maria Salomea Skłodowska Curie (née Skłodowska; 7 November 1867 – 4 July 1934), better known as Marie Curie, was a Polish and naturalised-French physicist and chemist.
She shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with her husband, Pierre Curie, "for their joint researches on the radioactivity phenomena discovered by Professor Henri Becquerel".
photo: Photosynthesis was discovered in 1779 by Jan Ingenhousz who showed that plants need light, not just soil and water.
Plants usually convert light into chemical energy with a photosynthetic efficiency of 3–6%.
berlinwall: The Berlin Wall fell on 9 November 1989 during the Peaceful Revolution, marking the beginning of the destruction of the figurative Iron Curtain, as East Berlin transit restrictions were overwhelmed and discarded.
Construction of the Berlin Wall was commenced by the government of the GDR on 13 August 1961.
canberra: With an estimated population of 484,630 as of 2025, Canberra is Australia's largest inland city and the eighth-largest Australian city by population.
The capital city was founded and formally named as Canberra in 1913.
panama: The Panama Canal (Spanish: Canal de Panamá) is an artificial 82-kilometer (51-mile) waterway in Panama that connects the Caribbean Sea with the Pacific Ocean.
Annual traffic has risen from about 1,000 ships in 1914, when the canal opened, to 14,702 vessels in 2008, for a total of 333.7 million Panama Canal/Universal Measurement System (PC/UMS) tons.
suez: The 193.3-kilometre-long (120.1-mile) canal is a key trade route between Europe and Asia.
Construction took 11 years, and the canal opened on 17 November 1869.
titanic: RMS Titanic sank in the North Atlantic Ocean on 15 April 1912.
Of the 2,208 passengers and crew aboard, approximately 1,500 died (estimates vary), making the incident one of the deadliest peacetime sinkings of a single ship.
pisa: The height of the tower is 55.86 metres (183 feet 3 inches) from the ground on the low side and 56.67 m (185 ft 11 in) on the high side.
Construction of the tower occurred in three stages over 199 years.
